newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open little changed on Monday as dealers expect to market to trade sideways amid a lack of market-moving news.

New York arabica futures ended broadly lower in thin trade Friday, with September down 4.10 cents at 176.30 cents a lb after ranging from 182.00 to 175.50. December finished 3.05 cents lower at 157.25 cents, while the back months closed down 0.95 to 3.45.
The September/December switch narrowed to 19.05 cents, down from 20.10 cents at the close Thursday.

Technically, traders said September support was seen near 174.25 cents. They said September may initially find some resistance at 179.00 cents, with a stronger upside hurdle seen at 184.50 cents -- a double top on the charts.
After Friday's close, however, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 2,183 60-kg bags as of July 24, to 92,828 bags. An additional 3,738 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

On the weather front, Weather Services Corp said today there is no damaging cold weather expected this week in Brazil's coffee belt, with low temperatures in the 50s to low 60s F (low to middle teens C).

London coffee futures were flat to firmer early Monday in thin, rangebound trade. At the midday break, September unchanged, at $1,590, after ranging from $1,600 to $1,585. November rose $3, to $1,584.
